environment.description: Same Lambda and Step Functions workflow deployed in EKS namespace 'workflow-processing'. Istio 1.19 service mesh with mTLS STRICT mode. An AuthorizationPolicy resource is applied at the namespace level: spec.rules allow traffic ONLY from principals in 'sa://cluster.local/ns/orchestrator/sa/step-functions-invoker'. A second AuthorizationPolicy with an empty rules list (deny-all baseline) is applied to the 'workflow-processing' namespace with action DENY for any source NOT matching the orchestrator namespace service account. The API Gateway endpoint routes through an internal NLB whose target group is the Istio ingress gateway in the 'orchestrator' namespace — however, external traffic arriving at the gateway is assigned the 'istio-ingressgateway' service account identity (not the 'step-functions-invoker' SA), meaning it fails the AuthorizationPolicy check. Only the Step Functions activity poller running as a pod in the 'orchestrator' namespace with the correct SA can reach the decryption endpoint. An attacker performing a padding oracle attack requires ~128 requests per byte × 16 bytes per block minimum, all of which would be rejected at the Envoy sidecar level with a 403 RBAC denial before reaching the Lambda function.

config.ingress_routing: External traffic enters via istio-ingressgateway SA identity, not step-functions-invoker SA
config.api_gateway: Internal NLB, routed through Istio ingress in orchestrator namespace
config.network_policy: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricting ingress to workflow-processing pods from orchestrator namespace only
